name: Paul
summary: A man from Tarsus, first called Saul, who attacked the church until Jesus spoke to him on the road to Damascus. He became an apostle who carried the gospel to the Gentiles in many lands and wrote many letters to the churches.

key_moments.title: Persecuting the Church
key_moments.description: When Stephen was stoned, the witnesses laid their clothes at the feet of a young man named Saul, who agreed with his death. Then Saul tore through the church, going into house after house and dragging men and women off to prison.

key_moments.title: Meets Jesus on the Road to Damascus
key_moments.description: Near Damascus a light shone from heaven around Saul, and Jesus asked him why he was persecuting Him. Saul was blind for three days, until Ananias laid hands on him; then he could see again and was baptized.

key_moments.title: Singing in Prison
key_moments.description: After Paul cast a spirit out of a fortune-telling girl, her masters had Paul and Silas beaten and locked in the stocks. At midnight they prayed and sang praises to God, and after an earthquake the jailer and his whole household believed and were baptized.

key_moments.title: Shipwrecked on the Way to Rome
key_moments.description: In a great storm at sea, Paul told the crew that an angel of God had promised not one of them would lose his life. The ship broke apart, but everyone reached land safely on the island of Melita.

key_moments.title: Preaching in Rome
key_moments.description: In Rome Paul was allowed to live by himself with a soldier guarding him. For two whole years he welcomed all who came to his rented house and boldly preached God's kingdom and the Lord Jesus Christ.
